notes.1-chronicles-16-34~endureth-for-ever: David delivering a psalm of thanksgiving to Asaph upon bringing the ark to Jerusalem.
notes.1-corinthians-10-13~way-to-escape: Paul assuring the church: God is faithful and will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able.
notes.1-corinthians-13-13~the-greatest-of-thes: Paul concluding the love chapter: 'now abideth faith, hope, charity, these three; but the greatest of these is charity'.
notes.1-corinthians-15-55~victory: Paul celebrating victory over death: 'O death, where is thy sting? O grave, where is thy victory?'
notes.1-john-1-9~unrighteousness: John assuring forgiveness: 'If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins'.
notes.1-john-4-19~because-he-first-loved: John explaining love's origin: 'We love him, because he first loved us'.
notes.1-kings-18-21~opinions: Elijah confronting Israel on Mount Carmel: 'How long halt ye between two opinions?'
notes.1-kings-19-12~still-small-voice: God revealing Himself to Elijah at Mount Horeb not in wind or quake, but in a still small voice.
notes.1-peter-5-7~careth: Peter counseling the scattered saints: 'Casting all your care upon him; for he careth for you'.
notes.1-samuel-15-22~fat-of-rams: Samuel rebuking king Saul: 'to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than fat of rams'.
notes.1-samuel-16-7~heart: The LORD instructing Samuel in Jesse's house: God looketh on the heart, not outward appearance.
notes.2-chronicles-7-14~heal-their-land: The LORD's covenant promise to Solomon for healing the land upon humble prayer and repentance.
notes.2-corinthians-12-9~weakness: The Lord to Paul concerning his thorn: 'My grace is sufficient for thee: for my strength is made perfect in weakness'.
notes.2-corinthians-5-17~creature: Paul on the new creation: 'if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature: old things are passed away'.
notes.2-kings-6-16~more-than-they-that: Elisha comforting his servant in Dothan: 'they that be with us are more than they that be with them'.
notes.2-samuel-22-2~deliverer: David's psalm of deliverance after being saved from Saul and all his enemies.
notes.2-samuel-7-12~set-up-thy-seed: Nathan the prophet conveying the Davidic covenant of an everlasting kingdom.
notes.2-timothy-1-7~sound-mind: Paul encouraging young Timothy: 'God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind'.
notes.2-timothy-3-16~inspiration-of-god: Paul confirming biblical authority: 'All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine'.
notes.acts-1-8~witnesses-unto-me: The risen Jesus commissioning the apostles: 'ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you'.
notes.acts-16-31~believe-on-the-lord: Paul and Silas answering the Philippian jailer: 'Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shalt be saved'.
notes.acts-4-12~must-be-saved: Peter declaring to the Sanhedrin: 'Neither is there salvation in any other: for there is none other name under heaven given among men'.
notes.colossians-3-23~heartily: Paul setting heavenly perspective: 'Set your affection on things above, not on things on the earth'.
notes.daniel-12-3~firmament: The angel revealing the end times: they that turn many to righteousness shall shine as the stars forever.
notes.deuteronomy-29-29~all-the-words-of: Moses distinguishing secret things belonging to God from revealed things given to Israel.
notes.deuteronomy-31-6~fail-thee-nor-forsake: Moses encouraging Israel before the Jordan crossing: the LORD will not fail nor forsake them.
notes.deuteronomy-6-5~might: The Great Shema given by Moses to Israel before entering Canaan: wholehearted love for God.
notes.ecclesiastes-12-13~whole-duty-of-man: The conclusion of the whole matter: 'Fear God, and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man'.
notes.ecclesiastes-3-1~purpose: Solomon observing divine timing: 'To every thing there is a season, and a time to every purpose'.
notes.ephesians-2-8~gift: Paul explaining salvation by grace through faith, not of works lest any man should boast.
notes.ephesians-4-32~as-god-for-christ: Paul urging kindness: 'be ye kind one to another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, even as God for Christ's sake hath forgiven you'.
notes.ephesians-6-11~wiles-of-the-devil: Paul on spiritual warfare: 'Put on the whole armour of God, that ye may be able to stand against the wiles of the devil'.
notes.esther-4-14~such-a-time-as: Mordecai challenging queen Esther: 'who knoweth whether thou art come to the kingdom for such a time as this?'
notes.exodus-14-14~hold-your-peace: Moses to trembling Israel before the Red Sea, proclaiming God will fight for them.
notes.exodus-20-3~before-me: The first commandment given to Israel at Mount Sinai, demanding exclusive worship of the LORD.
notes.exodus-3-14~i-am-that-i: God revealing His eternal self-existent name 'I AM THAT I AM' to Moses at the burning bush.
notes.exodus-33-14~i-will-give-thee: The LORD assuring Moses that His presence would go with him and give Israel rest.
notes.ezekiel-36-26~stony-heart: The LORD promising the new covenant: a new heart and a new spirit, replacing the stony heart.
notes.ezra-7-10~statutes-and-judgments: Ezra preparing his heart to seek the law of the LORD, do it, and teach statutes in Israel.
notes.galatians-2-20~liveth: Paul's testimony of union with Christ: 'I am crucified with Christ: nevertheless I live; yet not I, but Christ liveth in me'.
notes.galatians-5-22~longsuffering: Paul listing the fruit of the Spirit: love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith.
notes.genesis-1-1~heaven-and-the-earth: Moses to Israel in the wilderness: the absolute beginning and sovereignty of God over all creation.
notes.genesis-12-1~a-land-that-i: God calling Abram out of Haran into Canaan with the promise of a great nation.
notes.genesis-15-6~for-righteousness: Abram believing the LORD, credited to him for righteousness before circumcision.
notes.genesis-2-7~living-soul: Moses recording the creation of man from the dust with the breath of life given by God.
notes.genesis-22-8~god-will-provide-himself: Abraham answering Isaac on Mount Moriah, prophesying God providing Himself a lamb.
notes.genesis-28-15~whither-thou-goest: The LORD assuring Jacob at Bethel that He will be with him and bring him back to the land.
notes.genesis-50-20~alive: Joseph to his brothers in Egypt, declaring God's sovereign providence over human malice.
notes.genesis-9-13~bow: God's covenant with Noah and all creation following the flood, setting the bow in the cloud.
notes.habakkuk-2-4~faith: The prophet's foundational principle quoted throughout the epistles: 'the just shall live by his faith'.
notes.hebrews-11-1~evidence: The definition of faith: 'the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen'.
notes.hebrews-12-1~beset: The author exhorting believers: laying aside every weight and running with patience the race set before us.
notes.hebrews-12-2~the-author-and-finisher: The author focusing our gaze: 'Looking unto Jesus the author and finisher of our faith'.
notes.hebrews-4-12~twoedged-sword: The author describing scripture: 'the word of God is quick, and powerful, and sharper than any twoedged sword'.
notes.isaiah-26-3~stayed: Isaiah praising God: 'Thou wilt keep him in perfect peace, whose mind is stayed on thee'.
notes.isaiah-40-31~eagles: Isaiah encouraging exiles: 'they that wait upon the LORD shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings'.
notes.isaiah-53-5~bruised: Isaiah describing the Suffering Servant: 'He was wounded for our transgressions, he was bruised for our iniquities'.
notes.isaiah-55-6~call-ye-upon-him: Isaiah extending the gospel invitation: 'Seek ye the LORD while he may be found, call ye upon him while he is near'.
notes.isaiah-6-8~here-am-i-send: Isaiah responding to the Lord's call in the temple vision: 'Here am I; send me'.
notes.isaiah-7-14~call-his-name-immanuel: Isaiah giving king Ahaz the sign of the virgin birth of Immanuel.
notes.isaiah-9-6~prince-of-peace: Isaiah foretelling the birth of the Prince of Peace who shall reign upon David's throne.
notes.james-1-22~deceiving: James warning against deception: 'be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only'.
notes.jeremiah-29-11~expected-end: Jeremiah's letter to exiles in Babylon: 'I know the thoughts that I think toward you, saith the LORD, thoughts of peace'.
notes.jeremiah-33-3~mighty-things: The LORD in the court of the prison: 'Call unto me, and I will answer thee, and shew thee great and mighty things'.
notes.job-19-25~latter-day: Job's triumphant confession in agony: 'I know that my redeemer liveth, and shall stand at the latter day'.
notes.job-23-10~i-shall-come-forth: Job trusting God's testing: 'when he hath tried me, I shall come forth as gold'.
notes.job-38-4~i-laid-the-foundations: The LORD answering Job out of the whirlwind: 'Where wast thou when I laid the foundations of the earth?'
notes.john-1-14~full-of-grace-and: The incarnation of the Son of God: 'And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us'.
notes.john-1-1~was-god: John opening the Gospel: 'In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God'.
notes.john-10-10~more-abundantly: Jesus contrasting the thief: 'I am come that they might have life, and that they might have it more abundantly'.
notes.john-11-25~yet-shall-he-live: Jesus comforting Martha at Lazarus' tomb: 'I am the resurrection, and the life'.
notes.john-14-6~but-by-me: Jesus answering Thomas: 'I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me'.
notes.john-15-5~nothing: Jesus teaching the Vine and branches: 'without me ye can do nothing'.
notes.john-3-16~everlasting-life: Jesus to Nicodemus: 'For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son'.
notes.joshua-1-9~dismayed: The LORD charging Joshua to be strong and courageous taking command after Moses' death.
notes.joshua-24-15~serve-the-lord: Joshua's farewell challenge at Shechem: 'as for me and my house, we will serve the LORD'.
notes.judges-5-31~might: The song of Deborah and Barak celebrating the victory over Sisera and the might of God's people.
notes.judges-6-12~valour: The Angel of the LORD greeting Gideon hiding in the winepress as a 'mighty man of valour'.
notes.lamentations-3-22~compassions: Jeremiah amidst Jerusalem's ruins: 'It is of the LORD's mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not'.
notes.leviticus-17-11~atonement: The law of atonement: the life of the flesh is in the blood given upon the altar.
notes.leviticus-19-18~i-am-the-lord: The law of holiness given to Israel, commanding love of neighbour as oneself.
notes.luke-1-37~impossible: Gabriel assuring Mary at the Annunciation: 'For with God nothing shall be impossible'.
notes.luke-19-10~that-which-was-lost: Jesus in Zacchaeus' house: 'For the Son of man is come to seek and to save that which was lost'.
notes.luke-2-14~good-will-toward-men: The heavenly host praising God at Bethlehem: 'Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, good will toward men'.
notes.malachi-3-10~windows-of-heaven: The LORD challenging Israel to bring all tithes into the storehouse and prove His open windows of heaven.
notes.mark-10-45~a-ransom-for-many: Jesus defining His mission: 'For even the Son of man came not to be ministered unto, but to minister, and to give his life a ransom for many'.
notes.mark-8-36~lose-his-own-soul: Jesus warning His disciples: 'For what shall it profit a man, if he shall gain the whole world, and lose his own soul?'
notes.matthew-11-28~rest: Jesus extending the great invitation: 'Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest'.
notes.matthew-28-19~teach-all-nations: The Great Commission: 'Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost'.
notes.matthew-5-3~theirs-is-the-kingdom: Jesus opening the Sermon on the Mount with the Beatitudes: 'Blessed are the poor in spirit'.
notes.matthew-6-33~added: Jesus teaching against anxiety: 'Seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness'.
notes.micah-6-8~humbly: Micah summarizing God's requirement: 'to do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy God'.
notes.nehemiah-8-10~joy-of-the-lord: Nehemiah and Ezra encouraging the weeping people: 'the joy of the LORD is your strength'.
notes.numbers-23-19~repent: Balaam's oracle before Balak, declaring God cannot lie nor repent of His word.
notes.numbers-6-24~bless-thee-and-keep: The Aaronic priestly blessing ordained by God to place His name upon the children of Israel.
notes.philippians-1-6~the-day-of-jesus: Paul expressing confidence: He which hath begun a good work in you will perform it until the day of Jesus Christ.
notes.philippians-4-13~strengtheneth: Paul declaring strength: 'I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me'.
notes.philippians-4-6~requests-be-made-known: Paul counseling peace: 'Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known'.
notes.proverbs-18-10~safe: Solomon on divine security: 'The name of the LORD is a strong tower: the righteous runneth into it, and is safe'.
notes.proverbs-27-17~countenance: Solomon on fellowship: 'Iron sharpeneth iron; so a man sharpeneth the countenance of his friend'.
notes.proverbs-3-5~thine-own-understanding: Solomon instructing his son: 'Trust in the LORD with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding'.
notes.proverbs-4-23~issues-of-life: Solomon's counsel on vigilance: 'Keep thy heart with all diligence; for out of it are the issues of life'.
notes.proverbs-9-10~the-knowledge-of-the: The foundational wisdom principle: 'The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom'.
notes.psalm-1-1~seat-of-the-scornful: David describing the blessed man who delights in the law of the LORD rather than wicked counsel.
notes.psalm-103-1~bless-his-holy-name: David commanding his soul to bless the LORD and forget not all His benefits.
notes.psalm-118-24~rejoice-and-be-glad: The festive psalm of praise: 'This is the day which the LORD hath made; we will rejoice and be glad in it'.
notes.psalm-119-105~light: The psalmist praising the Word: 'Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path'.
notes.psalm-121-1~help: The Song of Degrees: lifting eyes unto the hills, knowing help cometh from the LORD.
notes.psalm-139-14~marvellous: David praising God's omniscient workmanship: 'I am fearfully and wonderfully made'.
notes.psalm-19-1~handywork: David celebrating general revelation: 'The heavens declare the glory of God; and the firmament sheweth his handywork'.
notes.psalm-23-1~not-want: David resting in the LORD as his faithful Shepherd providing in green pastures and the valley of shadow.
notes.psalm-27-1~strength: David declaring the LORD his light and salvation, dispelling all fear in time of trouble.
notes.psalm-34-8~taste-and-see: David praising God after feigning madness before Abimelech: 'O taste and see that the LORD is good'.
notes.psalm-37-4~desires-of-thine-heart: David counseling trust: 'Delight thyself also in the LORD; and he shall give thee the desires of thine heart'.
notes.psalm-46-10~i-will-be-exalted: God commanding the nations: 'Be still, and know that I am God: I will be exalted in the earth'.
notes.psalm-46-1~help: The sons of Korah singing of God as refuge, strength, and a very present help in trouble.
notes.psalm-51-10~right-spirit: David's penitential prayer after his sin with Bathsheba: 'Create in me a clean heart, O God'.
notes.psalm-90-12~wisdom: Moses praying: 'So teach us to number our days, that we may apply our hearts unto wisdom'.
notes.psalm-91-1~abide: The psalm of refuge: dwelling in the secret place of the most High under the shadow of the Almighty.
notes.revelation-21-4~former-things: The glorious promise of the New Jerusalem: God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes; and there shall be no more death.
notes.revelation-3-20~sup: Jesus to the church in Laodicea: 'Behold, I stand at the door, and knock: if any man hear my voice, and open the door, I will come in'.
notes.romans-1-16~also-to-the-greek: Paul declaring his confidence: 'For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ: for it is the power of God unto salvation'.
notes.romans-10-9~saved: Paul explaining the word of faith: confessing the Lord Jesus and believing in the heart that God raised Him.
notes.romans-12-1~your-reasonable-service: Paul urging consecration: presenting bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto God.
notes.romans-12-2~renewing: Paul on renewal: 'be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind'.
notes.romans-3-23~glory: Paul establishing universal need: 'For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God'.
notes.romans-5-8~for-us: Paul demonstrating divine love: 'God commendeth his love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us'.
notes.romans-6-23~eternal-life: Paul contrasting sin and grace: 'For the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord'.
notes.romans-8-28~purpose: Paul assuring believers: 'all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose'.
notes.ruth-1-16~thy-god-my-god: Ruth's steadfast covenant vow of loyalty to Naomi and Naomi's God on the road to Bethlehem.
notes.zechariah-4-6~lord-of-hosts: The word of the LORD unto Zerubbabel: 'Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, saith the LORD of hosts'.

tfClaims.s: Sarah was Abraham's wife.
tfClaims.why: God said: Sarah thy wife shall bear thee a son (Genesis 17:15-19).

tfClaims.s: Joseph's brothers sold him to the Ishmeelites for twenty pieces of silver.
tfClaims.why: They sold Joseph to the Ishmeelites for twenty pieces of silver (Genesis 37:28).

tfClaims.s: Benjamin was Rachel's son.
tfClaims.why: Benjamin was born of Rachel on the way to Ephrath (Genesis 35:16-18).

tfClaims.s: Adam called his wife's name Eve.
tfClaims.why: Adam called his wife's name Eve, because she was the mother of all living (Genesis 3:20).

tfClaims.s: Pharaoh set Joseph over all the land of Egypt.
tfClaims.why: Pharaoh said: thou shalt be over my house — without thee shall no man lift up his hand (Genesis 41:41-44).

tfClaims.s: Lot was Abraham's brother.
tfClaims.why: Lot was Abram's nephew — his brother Haran's son (Genesis 12:5).

tfClaims.s: Jacob was Isaac's father.
tfClaims.why: Isaac was Jacob's father — the elder bore the younger (Genesis 25:26).

tfClaims.s: Abel rose up against Cain and slew him.
tfClaims.why: Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him (Genesis 4:8).

tfClaims.s: The ark rested upon the mountains of Sinai.
tfClaims.why: The ark rested upon the mountains of Ararat (Genesis 8:4).

tfClaims.s: Eve was formed before Adam.
tfClaims.why: Adam was formed first, then Eve — the rib taken from his side (Genesis 2:7, 21-22).

tfClaims.s: Esau sold his birthright for gold.
tfClaims.why: He sold it for bread and pottage of lentiles (Genesis 25:33-34).

tfClaims.s: Isaac blessed Esau with the firstborn blessing.
tfClaims.why: Jacob obtained the blessing of the firstborn through subtle deception (Genesis 27:35-36).

tfClaims.s: The forbidden fruit in Eden is identified in Genesis as an apple.
tfClaims.why: Genesis names only the fruit of the tree of knowledge — no apple is ever mentioned (Genesis 3:3-6).

tfClaims.s: Melchizedek was king of Salem and priest of the most high God.
tfClaims.why: Melchizedek king of Salem brought forth bread and wine (Genesis 14:18).

tfClaims.s: Rebekah was the sister of Laban.
tfClaims.why: Rebekah had a brother, and his name was Laban (Genesis 24:29).

tfClaims.s: Noah took two of every clean beast into the ark.
tfClaims.why: Clean beasts came in by sevens — two was the rule for unclean (Genesis 7:2).

tfClaims.s: Rachel was Jacob's daughter.
tfClaims.why: Rachel was Jacob's wife, given him in Haran (Genesis 29:28).

tfClaims.s: Haran was Lot's son.
tfClaims.why: Haran was Lot's father — Haran begat Lot (Genesis 11:27).

tfClaims.s: Leah was younger than Rachel.
tfClaims.why: Leah was the elder and Rachel the younger (Genesis 29:16).

tfClaims.s: Ishmael was born of Sarah.
tfClaims.why: Ishmael was the son of Hagar the Egyptian handmaid (Genesis 16:15).

tfClaims.s: Abraham was seventy years old when Isaac was born.
tfClaims.why: Abraham was an hundred years old when his son Isaac was born (Genesis 21:5).

tfClaims.s: Joseph had ten brothers in total.
tfClaims.why: Jacob had twelve sons — Joseph had eleven brothers (Genesis 35:22).

tfClaims.s: Cain was a keeper of sheep and Abel was a tiller of the ground.
tfClaims.why: Abel was a keeper of sheep, but Cain was a tiller of the ground (Genesis 4:2).

tfClaims.s: Joseph gave Benjamin five changes of raiment and three pieces of gold.
tfClaims.why: He gave him three hundred pieces of silver, and five changes of raiment (Genesis 45:22).

tfClaims.s: Methuselah lived nine hundred sixty and nine years.
tfClaims.why: And all the days of Methuselah were nine hundred sixty and nine years: and he died (Genesis 5:27).

tfClaims.s: Judah pledged his life for Benjamin before Joseph.
tfClaims.why: Judah said: I will be surety for him; of my hand shalt thou require him (Genesis 43:9).

tfClaims.s: Enoch died and was buried by Adam.
tfClaims.why: Enoch walked with God: and he was not; for God took him (Genesis 5:24).

tfClaims.s: Terah died in Ur of the Chaldees.
tfClaims.why: Terah died in Haran after journeying from Ur (Genesis 11:31-32).

tfClaims.s: Miriam was Aaron's sister.
tfClaims.why: Miriam the prophetess, sister to Aaron, led the women with timbrels (Exodus 15:20).

tfClaims.s: The golden calf was fashioned by Aaron.
tfClaims.why: Aaron fashioned it with a graving tool of the people's golden earrings (Exodus 32:2-4).

tfClaims.s: Moses was drawn out of the water by Pharaoh's daughter.
tfClaims.why: She called his name Moses — drawn out of the water (Exodus 2:5-10).

tfClaims.s: Moses was Jethro's father.
tfClaims.why: Jethro was Moses' father in law, priest of Midian (Exodus 3:1).

tfClaims.s: Aaron was Moses' son.
tfClaims.why: Aaron was Moses' brother — his mouth in Egypt (Exodus 4:14; 7:1).

tfClaims.s: Egypt was smitten with seven plagues.
tfClaims.why: Ten plagues fell — from blood to the death of the firstborn (Exodus 7-12).

tfClaims.s: Israel ate manna in the wilderness for twenty years.
tfClaims.why: Israel did eat manna forty years, until they came to Canaan's border (Exodus 16:35).

tfClaims.s: Pharaoh commanded all Hebrew baby girls to be drowned in the river.
tfClaims.why: Every son that is born ye shall cast into the river — girls were saved alive (Exodus 1:22).

tfClaims.s: Pharaoh drowned in the Red Sea alongside his chariots.
tfClaims.why: The scriptures state that the waters covered the chariots and horsemen, but never explicitly state Pharaoh himself drowned (Exodus 14:28).

tfClaims.s: The first plague upon Egypt was frogs in all the houses.
tfClaims.why: The first plague was turning all the waters of Egypt into blood (Exodus 7:20).

tfClaims.s: Moses was fourscore years old when he spake unto Pharaoh.
tfClaims.why: Aaron was three and eighty, and Moses fourscore, when they spake unto Pharaoh (Exodus 7:7).

tfClaims.s: The LORD led Israel by a pillar of cloud by day and fire by night.
tfClaims.why: The LORD went before them by day in a pillar of a cloud, and by night in a pillar of fire (Exodus 13:21).

tfClaims.s: The tabernacle was built by Moses's own hands alone.
tfClaims.why: Bezaleel and Aholiab were filled with the spirit to build it (Exodus 31:1-6).

tfClaims.s: The bush burned with fire and was consumed.
tfClaims.why: Behold, the bush burned with fire, and the bush was not consumed (Exodus 3:2).

tfClaims.s: The Israelites dwelt in Egypt fourscore years.
tfClaims.why: The sojourning of the children of Israel in Egypt was four hundred and thirty years (Exodus 12:40).

tfClaims.s: The ark of the covenant was placed in the outer court of the tabernacle.
tfClaims.why: It was placed in the most holy place within the vail (Exodus 26:33-34).

tfClaims.s: Aaron was forty days in Mount Sinai with the LORD.
tfClaims.why: Moses went into the midst of the cloud, and was in the mount forty days (Exodus 24:18).

tfClaims.s: Hur and Aaron held up Moses' hands at Rephidim.
tfClaims.why: Aaron and Hur stayed up his hands, the one on the one side, and the other on the other side (Exodus 17:12).

tfClaims.s: Moses' rod became a lion before Pharaoh.
tfClaims.why: Cast it before Pharaoh, and it shall become a serpent (Exodus 7:9).

tfClaims.s: Nadab and Abihu offered strange fire before the LORD.
tfClaims.why: Nadab and Abihu offered strange fire before the LORD, and there went out fire and devoured them (Leviticus 10:1-2).

tfClaims.s: The high priest entered the most holy place once every year on the Day of Atonement.
tfClaims.why: Once in the year shall he make atonement upon the horns of it (Leviticus 16:34; Exodus 30:10).

tfClaims.s: Nadab and Abihu were sons of Moses.
tfClaims.why: Nadab and Abihu were the sons of Aaron the high priest (Leviticus 10:1).

tfClaims.s: The scapegoat was sent away by the hand of a fit man into the wilderness.
tfClaims.why: He shall let go the goat in the wilderness... into a land not inhabited (Leviticus 16:21-22).

tfClaims.s: The jubilee year was proclaimed every seventh year.
tfClaims.why: The fiftieth year was the jubilee — not every seventh (Leviticus 25:10-11).

tfClaims.s: The LORD opened the mouth of Balaam's ass.
tfClaims.why: The ass saw the angel, and the LORD opened her mouth to speak (Numbers 22:28).

tfClaims.s: The spies searched the land of Canaan forty days.
tfClaims.why: They returned from searching after forty days, bearing the cluster of Eschol (Numbers 13:25).

tfClaims.s: Israel wandered in the wilderness twenty years.
tfClaims.why: Forty years — a year for each day of searching (Numbers 14:33-34).

tfClaims.s: Aaron's rod budded and brought forth almonds.
tfClaims.why: Behold, the rod of Aaron for the house of Levi was budded... and yielded almonds (Numbers 17:8).

tfClaims.s: Korah and his company were swallowed by the earth.
tfClaims.why: The earth opened her mouth, and swallowed them up, and their houses (Numbers 16:32).

tfClaims.s: Moses sent twenty-four spies into the land of Canaan.
tfClaims.why: Twelve spies were sent — one from each tribe of Israel (Numbers 13:2-4).

tfClaims.s: Balaam blessed Balak and cursed Israel.
tfClaims.why: God turned the curse into a blessing — Balaam could only bless Israel (Numbers 23:11-12).

tfClaims.s: Moses set up a brazen eagle upon a pole.
tfClaims.why: Moses made a serpent of brass, and put it upon a pole (Numbers 21:9).

tfClaims.s: Balaam struck his ass five times before the LORD opened her mouth.
tfClaims.why: Balaam smote her three times (Numbers 22:28).

tfClaims.s: Joshua was full of the spirit of wisdom when Moses laid hands on him.
tfClaims.why: Moses laid his hands upon him, and Israel hearkened unto him (Deuteronomy 34:9).

tfClaims.s: Moses entered the land of Canaan with Israel.
tfClaims.why: Moses died in Moab upon Nebo, and was buried by the LORD — he saw the land, but did not cross (Deuteronomy 34:5).

tfClaims.s: Moses died on Mount Nebo at the age of one hundred and twenty years.
tfClaims.why: Moses was an hundred and twenty years old when he died: his eye was not dim (Deuteronomy 34:7).

tfClaims.s: The blessings of obedience were pronounced from Mount Ebal and curses from Mount Gerizim.
tfClaims.why: Blessings from Mount Gerizim, and curses from Mount Ebal (Deuteronomy 27:12-13).

tfClaims.s: Moses died in the land of Canaan on Mount Carmel.
tfClaims.why: Moses died in Moab upon Mount Nebo (Deuteronomy 34:1, 5).

tfClaims.s: Og king of Bashan had a bedstead of iron.
tfClaims.why: Behold, his bedstead was a bedstead of iron; is it not in Rabbath of the children of Ammon? (Deuteronomy 3:11).

tfClaims.s: Moses' grave in the valley in the land of Moab is known to this day.
tfClaims.why: No man knoweth of his sepulchre unto this day (Deuteronomy 34:6).

tfClaims.s: Rahab hid the two spies upon the roof of her house.
tfClaims.why: She hid them with stalks of flax upon the roof (Joshua 2:4-6).

tfClaims.s: Achan took of the accursed thing at Jericho.
tfClaims.why: Achan took of the accursed thing, and Israel fell before Ai (Joshua 7:1).

tfClaims.s: Jericho's wall fell on the third day of circling.
tfClaims.why: On the seventh day they compassed the city seven times, and the wall fell (Joshua 6:15, 20).

tfClaims.s: Joshua was Moses' father.
tfClaims.why: Joshua was the son of Nun, Moses' minister (Joshua 1:1).

tfClaims.s: The sun stood still upon Gibeon at Joshua's command.
tfClaims.why: Sun, stand thou still upon Gibeon; and thou, Moon, in the valley of Ajalon (Joshua 10:12).

tfClaims.s: Caleb asked Joshua for the mountain of Hebron when he was eighty and five years old.
tfClaims.why: Now therefore give me this mountain... I am this day fourscore and five years old (Joshua 14:10-12).

tfClaims.s: The Gibeonites made peace with Joshua by threatening him with an army.
tfClaims.why: They worked wilily with old sacks, rent bottles, and mouldy bread (Joshua 9:4-6).

tfClaims.s: Joshua set up thirty-six stones in Gilgal.
tfClaims.why: Those twelve stones, which they took out of Jordan, did Joshua pitch in Gilgal (Joshua 4:20).

tfClaims.s: The city of Ai fell on the first attack by three thousand men.
tfClaims.why: Israel fled before the men of Ai because of Achan's sin (Joshua 7:4-5).

tfClaims.s: The stones taken from Jordan were pitched at Shiloh.
tfClaims.why: Those twelve stones, which they took out of Jordan, did Joshua pitch in Gilgal (Joshua 4:20).

tfClaims.s: Samson slew a thousand men with the jawbone of an ass.
tfClaims.why: With the jawbone he slew a thousand men, and called the place Ramath-lehi (Judges 15:15-17).

tfClaims.s: Deborah was a prophetess and a judge of Israel.
tfClaims.why: Deborah, a prophetess, judged Israel at that time under a palm tree (Judges 4:4-5).

tfClaims.s: Gideon went to battle with thirty thousand men.
tfClaims.why: The LORD cut the army to three hundred men with lamps and trumpets (Judges 7:7, 16).

tfClaims.s: Delilah cut Samson's hair with her own hands.
tfClaims.why: She called for a man, and caused him to shave off his seven locks (Judges 16:19).

tfClaims.s: Jael drove a tent nail into Sisera's temples.
tfClaims.why: Jael took a nail of the tent, and smote the nail into his temples (Judges 4:21).

tfClaims.s: Barak went to war against Sisera without Deborah.
tfClaims.why: Barak said unto her, If thou wilt go with me, then I will go (Judges 4:8).

tfClaims.s: Samson told Delilah the secret of his strength on her first request.
tfClaims.why: He mocked her three times with green withs, new ropes, and weaving the locks of his head (Judges 16:7-14).

tfClaims.s: Gideon was from the tribe of Judah.
tfClaims.why: My family is poor in Manasseh, and I am the least in my father's house (Judges 6:15).

tfClaims.s: Ehud was left-handed and slew Eglon king of Moab.
tfClaims.why: The LORD raised them up a deliverer, Ehud... a man lefthanded (Judges 3:15).

tfClaims.s: Shamgar slew six hundred Philistines with an ox goad.
tfClaims.why: Shamgar the son of Anath, which slew of the Philistines six hundred men with an ox goad (Judges 3:31).

tfClaims.s: Ruth was Naomi's daughter in law.
tfClaims.why: Ruth the Moabitess clave unto her, and returned with her to Bethlehem (Ruth 1:22).

tfClaims.s: Boaz was Ruth's brother.
tfClaims.why: Boaz took Ruth to wife, and Obed was born of the union (Ruth 4:13).

tfClaims.s: Ruth was a native of Bethlehem.
tfClaims.why: Ruth was a Moabitess — she came to Bethlehem with Naomi (Ruth 1:22).

tfClaims.s: Obed, Ruth's son, was the grandfather of David.
tfClaims.why: Obed begat Jesse, and Jesse begat David (Ruth 4:17).

tfClaims.s: Orpah returned to Moab while Ruth clave to Naomi.
tfClaims.why: Orpah kissed her mother in law; but Ruth clave unto her (Ruth 1:14).

tfClaims.s: Naomi's husband was named Boaz.
tfClaims.why: The name of the man was Elimelech, and the name of his wife Naomi (Ruth 1:2).

tfClaims.s: Jonathan was Saul's son.
tfClaims.why: Jonathan, Saul's son, delighted much in David (1 Samuel 19:1-2).

tfClaims.s: David told Saul he had slain both a lion and a bear.
tfClaims.why: Thy servant slew both the lion and the bear (1 Samuel 17:36).

tfClaims.s: Hannah brought young Samuel to the house of the LORD in Shiloh.
tfClaims.why: Hannah brought him unto the house of the LORD in Shiloh: and the child was young (1 Samuel 1:24).

tfClaims.s: David slew Goliath with a sword.
tfClaims.why: David slew him with a sling and a stone — the sword was only used to take off his head (1 Samuel 17:49-51).

tfClaims.s: Eli was high priest in Jerusalem.
tfClaims.why: Eli judged Israel and ministered in Shiloh before the temple existed (1 Samuel 1:3).

tfClaims.s: The ark of God was taken by the Philistines when Hophni and Phinehas died.
tfClaims.why: The ark of God was taken; and the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, were slain (1 Samuel 4:11).

tfClaims.s: Goliath was a giant of Ashdod.
tfClaims.why: Goliath of Gath, six cubits and a span (1 Samuel 17:4).

tfClaims.s: David was Saul's grandson.
tfClaims.why: David became Saul's son in law, given Michal to wife (1 Samuel 18:27-28).

tfClaims.s: Saul was from the tribe of Judah.
tfClaims.why: Saul was the son of Kish, a Benjamite (1 Samuel 9:1-2).

tfClaims.s: David was the eldest son of Jesse.
tfClaims.why: David was the youngest of eight sons (1 Samuel 16:10-11).

tfClaims.s: Goliath fell backward when the stone struck his forehead.
tfClaims.why: The stone sunk into his forehead; and he fell upon his face to the earth (1 Samuel 17:49).

tfClaims.s: Jonathan threw a spear at David to kill him.
tfClaims.why: Saul cast a javelin at David — Jonathan loved David as his own soul (1 Samuel 18:11; 20:17).

tfClaims.s: Abigail brought provisions to David when Nabal refused him.
tfClaims.why: Abigail made haste, and took two hundred loaves... and met David (1 Samuel 25:18).

tfClaims.s: Dagon the idol fell on his face before the ark of the LORD in Ashdod.
tfClaims.why: Dagon was fallen upon his face to the earth before the ark of the LORD (1 Samuel 5:3).

tfClaims.s: David was anointed king over Judah in Hebron.
tfClaims.why: The men of Judah came, and there they anointed David king over the house of Judah (2 Samuel 2:4).

tfClaims.s: Absalom's head caught in an oak tree.
tfClaims.why: His head caught hold of the oak, and he was taken up between the heaven and the earth (2 Samuel 18:9).

tfClaims.s: Uzzah put forth his hand to the ark of God and died.
tfClaims.why: Uzzah put forth his hand to the ark of God... and God smote him there (2 Samuel 6:6-7).

tfClaims.s: Nathan rebuked David with the parable of the ewe lamb.
tfClaims.why: Nathan said to David, Thou art the man (2 Samuel 12:1-7).

tfClaims.s: Uriah the Hittite was David's general who commanded the army.
tfClaims.why: Joab was the captain of the host; Uriah was one of the thirty mighty men (2 Samuel 8:16; 23:39).

tfClaims.s: Benaiah the son of Jehoiada slew a lion in the midst of a pit in time of snow.
tfClaims.why: He went down also and slew a lion in the midst of a pit in time of snow (2 Samuel 23:20).

tfClaims.s: Joab was David's father.
tfClaims.why: Joab was David's nephew, the son of Zeruiah (2 Samuel 2:18).

tfClaims.s: Solomon asked God for an understanding heart to judge the people.
tfClaims.why: Give therefore thy servant an understanding heart to judge thy people (1 Kings 3:9).

tfClaims.s: Solomon built the ark of the covenant.
tfClaims.why: Bezaleel made the ark in the wilderness; Solomon built the temple that housed it (Exodus 37:1; 1 Kings 6).

tfClaims.s: The queen of Sheba came to prove David with hard questions.
tfClaims.why: She came to prove Solomon with hard questions at Jerusalem (1 Kings 10:1).

tfClaims.s: Solomon's temple was seven years in building.
tfClaims.why: He was seven years in building it (1 Kings 6:38).

tfClaims.s: Jeroboam set up two calves of gold, one in Bethel and the other in Dan.
tfClaims.why: He set the one in Beth-el, and the other put he in Dan (1 Kings 12:28-29).

tfClaims.s: Elijah called down fire on Mount Carmel against the prophets of Baal.
tfClaims.why: The fire of the LORD fell, and consumed the burnt sacrifice (1 Kings 18:38).

tfClaims.s: Elijah confronted four hundred and fifty prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel.
tfClaims.why: The prophets of Baal four hundred and fifty, and the prophets of the groves four hundred (1 Kings 18:19).

tfClaims.s: Rehoboam listened to the counsel of the old men.
tfClaims.why: He forsook the counsel of the old men and followed the young men (1 Kings 12:8-13).

tfClaims.s: Jezebel was the daughter of the king of Judah.
tfClaims.why: Jezebel was the daughter of Ethbaal king of the Zidonians (1 Kings 16:31).

tfClaims.s: The ravens fed Elijah with bread and flesh at the brook Cherith.
tfClaims.why: The ravens brought him bread and flesh in the morning, and bread and flesh in the evening (1 Kings 17:6).

tfClaims.s: Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven.
tfClaims.why: A chariot of fire parted them, and Elijah went up by a whirlwind (2 Kings 2:11).

tfClaims.s: Naaman the Syrian dipped himself six times in Jordan.
tfClaims.why: He dipped himself seven times, and his flesh came again like a child's (2 Kings 5:14).

tfClaims.s: Josiah was eight years old when he began to reign.
tfClaims.why: Josiah was eight years old when he began to reign (2 Kings 22:1).

tfClaims.s: An angel of the LORD slew 185,000 Assyrians in Sennacherib's camp in one night.
tfClaims.why: The angel of the LORD went out, and smote in the camp of the Assyrians an hundred fourscore and five thousand (2 Kings 19:35).

tfClaims.s: Elisha was taken up in a chariot of fire instead of Elijah.
tfClaims.why: Elijah went up in the whirlwind; Elisha took up his mantle (2 Kings 2:11-13).

tfClaims.s: Athaliah was a righteous queen who preserved the house of David.
tfClaims.why: She destroyed all the seed royal when her son Ahaziah died (2 Kings 11:1).

tfClaims.s: Gehazi was smitten with the leprosy of Naaman for his greed.
tfClaims.why: The leprosy therefore of Naaman shall cleave unto thee... and he went out a leper as white as snow (2 Kings 5:27).

tfClaims.s: Jabez prayed that God would enlarge his coast and keep him from evil.
tfClaims.why: Jabez called on the God of Israel, saying, Oh that thou wouldest bless me indeed (1 Chronicles 4:10).

tfClaims.s: David was not permitted to build the temple because he had shed much blood upon the earth.
tfClaims.why: Thou shalt not build an house unto my name, because thou hast shed much blood upon the earth (1 Chronicles 22:8).

tfClaims.s: Jehoshaphat sent singers before the army to praise the beauty of holiness.
tfClaims.why: He appointed singers unto the LORD... that should praise the beauty of holiness (2 Chronicles 20:21).

tfClaims.s: King Uzziah was struck with leprosy when he went into the temple to burn incense.
tfClaims.why: While he was wroth with the priests, the leprosy even rose up in his forehead (2 Chronicles 26:19).

tfClaims.s: Cyrus king of Persia made a decree to rebuild the house of God in Jerusalem.
tfClaims.why: Cyrus king of Persia made a proclamation... to build him an house at Jerusalem (Ezra 1:1-3).

tfClaims.s: Ezra was a ready scribe in the law of Moses.
tfClaims.why: This Ezra went up from Babylon; and he was a ready scribe in the law of Moses (Ezra 7:6).

tfClaims.s: Tattenai the governor tried to hinder the rebuilding of the temple in Jerusalem.
tfClaims.why: Tattenai, governor on this side the river, and Shethar-boznai... came unto them, and said thus unto them, Who hath commanded you to build? (Ezra 5:3).

tfClaims.s: Nehemiah was the king's cupbearer.
tfClaims.why: I was the king's cupbearer (Nehemiah 1:11).

tfClaims.s: The wall of Jerusalem was finished in fifty and two days.
tfClaims.why: So the wall was finished... in fifty and two days, notwithstanding the enemies' plots (Nehemiah 6:15).

tfClaims.s: Sanballat and Tobiah helped Nehemiah rebuild the wall.
tfClaims.why: Sanballat and Tobiah mocked and conspired to fight against Jerusalem (Nehemiah 4:1-8).

tfClaims.s: Ezra read the law from a pulpit of wood from morning until midday.
tfClaims.why: Ezra the scribe stood upon a pulpit of wood... and read therein from the morning until midday (Nehemiah 8:3-4).

tfClaims.s: Mordecai sat in the king's gate.
tfClaims.why: Mordecai sat in the king's gate, and discovered the plot of Bigthan and Teresh (Esther 2:19-21).

tfClaims.s: Esther was king Ahasuerus's daughter.
tfClaims.why: Ahasuerus made Esther queen in Vashti's place — his wife, not his daughter (Esther 2:17).

tfClaims.s: Haman was Esther's cousin.
tfClaims.why: Mordecai was her cousin — Haman was the Agagite who sought to destroy her people (Esther 2:7; 3:1).

tfClaims.s: Vashti obeyed the king's commandment to come before his princes.
tfClaims.why: Queen Vashti refused to come at the king's commandment (Esther 1:12).

tfClaims.s: Haman was hanged on the gallows he prepared for Mordecai.
tfClaims.why: So they hanged Haman on the gallows that he had prepared for Mordecai (Esther 7:10).

tfClaims.s: The feast of Purim was instituted to commemorate the Jews' deliverance in Persia.
tfClaims.why: They called these days Purim after the name of Pur (Esther 9:26-28).

tfClaims.s: Job's friends sat with him seven days and seven nights without speaking.
tfClaims.why: They sat down with him upon the ground seven days and seven nights, and none spake a word (Job 2:13).

tfClaims.s: Job cursed God to his face.
tfClaims.why: In all this Job sinned not, nor charged God foolishly (Job 1:22).

tfClaims.s: The LORD spoke to Job out of the whirlwind.
tfClaims.why: Then the LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind, and said (Job 38:1).

tfClaims.s: Elihu was the oldest of Job's four visitors.
tfClaims.why: Elihu was young, and they were very old; wherefore he waited to speak (Job 32:4-6).

tfClaims.s: Psalm 23 begins 'The LORD is my shepherd'.
tfClaims.why: The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want (Psalm 23:1).

tfClaims.s: Psalm 1 blesses the man who walks in the counsel of the ungodly.
tfClaims.why: Blessed is the man that walketh NOT in the counsel of the ungodly (Psalm 1:1).

tfClaims.s: Psalm 119 is the shortest chapter in the Bible.
tfClaims.why: Psalm 119 is the longest chapter in the Bible; Psalm 117 is the shortest (Psalm 117; Psalm 119).

tfClaims.s: David wrote every single psalm in the book of Psalms.
tfClaims.why: Psalms are authored by David, Asaph, the sons of Korah, Moses, and Solomon (Psalm 90:title; 72:20).

tfClaims.s: Psalm 90 is titled a prayer of Moses the man of God.
tfClaims.why: A Prayer of Moses the man of God — Lord, thou hast been our dwelling place (Psalm 90:1).

tfClaims.s: Asaph is named in the title of twelve psalms.
tfClaims.why: Psalm 50 and Psalms 73 through 83 bear the name of Asaph in their titles (Psalm 50:title; 73:title).

tfClaims.s: The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge.
tfClaims.why: The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge (Proverbs 1:7).

tfClaims.s: Proverbs teaches that a soft answer stirreth up wrath.
tfClaims.why: A soft answer turneth away wrath; grievous words stir up anger (Proverbs 15:1).

tfClaims.s: Proverbs 31 describes the virtuous woman.
tfClaims.why: Who can find a virtuous woman? for her price is far above rubies (Proverbs 31:10).

tfClaims.s: Ecclesiastes opens with 'vanity of vanities... all is vanity'.
tfClaims.why: Vanity of vanities, saith the Preacher, vanity of vanities; all is vanity (Ecclesiastes 1:2).

tfClaims.s: Ecclesiastes declares that a threefold cord is quickly broken.
tfClaims.why: A threefold cord is not quickly broken (Ecclesiastes 4:12).

tfClaims.s: The Song of Solomon describes love as strong as death.
tfClaims.why: For love is strong as death; jealousy is cruel as the grave (Song of Solomon 8:6).

tfClaims.s: The Rose of Sharon is mentioned in the Song of Solomon.
tfClaims.why: I am the rose of Sharon, and the lily of the valleys (Song of Solomon 2:1).

tfClaims.s: Isaiah saw the Lord on a throne in the year king Uzziah died.
tfClaims.why: In the year that king Uzziah died I saw also the Lord sitting upon a throne (Isaiah 6:1).

tfClaims.s: Isaiah prophesied that a virgin shall conceive and bear a son named Immanuel.
tfClaims.why: Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel (Isaiah 7:14).

tfClaims.s: Isaiah was three days and three nights in the fish's belly.
tfClaims.why: That was Jonah — Isaiah saw the Lord on His throne instead (Jonah 1:17; Isaiah 6:1).

tfClaims.s: A seraphim touched Isaiah's lips with a live coal from the altar.
tfClaims.why: Then flew one of the seraphims unto me, having a live coal in his hand (Isaiah 6:6-7).

tfClaims.s: Isaiah chapter 53 describes the Suffering Servant wounded for our transgressions.
tfClaims.why: He was wounded for our transgressions, he was bruised for our iniquities (Isaiah 53:5).

tfClaims.s: Cyrus is named by Isaiah more than a century before his birth.
tfClaims.why: That saith of Cyrus, He is my shepherd, and shall perform all my pleasure (Isaiah 44:28; 45:1).

tfClaims.s: Jeremiah was cast into a dungeon.
tfClaims.why: They let him down with cords into the dungeon of Malchiah — he sank in the mire (Jeremiah 38:6).

tfClaims.s: Jeremiah was carried to Babylon with the captives.
tfClaims.why: Jeremiah was left in the land with the poor, and later taken into Egypt (Jeremiah 39:11-12; 43:5-7).

tfClaims.s: Baruch was Jeremiah's scribe who wrote the words of the LORD from his mouth.
tfClaims.why: Jeremiah called Baruch the son of Neriah: and Baruch wrote from the mouth of Jeremiah (Jeremiah 36:4).

tfClaims.s: King Jehoiakim cut Jeremiah's scroll with a penknife and burned it.
tfClaims.why: He cut it with the penknife, and cast it into the fire that was on the hearth (Jeremiah 36:23).

tfClaims.s: Ebed-melech the Ethiopian drew Jeremiah out of the mire of the dungeon with rotten rags.
tfClaims.why: Ebed-melech... took old cast clouts and old rotten rags, and let them down by cords... into the dungeon (Jeremiah 38:11-13).

tfClaims.s: Lamentations proclaims that the LORD's compassions fail not and are new every morning.
tfClaims.why: His compassions fail not. They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness (Lamentations 3:22-23).

tfClaims.s: Lamentations is composed of five distinct poems matching its five chapters.
tfClaims.why: Each chapter is an independent lamentation poem in the Hebrew text (Lamentations 1-5).

tfClaims.s: Ezekiel prophesied to a valley of dry bones.
tfClaims.why: Prophesy upon these bones, and say unto them, O ye dry bones (Ezekiel 37:4).

tfClaims.s: Ezekiel was among the captives by the river of Chebar.
tfClaims.why: As I was among the captives by the river of Chebar, the heavens were opened (Ezekiel 1:1).

tfClaims.s: Ezekiel was commanded to eat a scroll sweet as honey.
tfClaims.why: Then did I eat it; and it was in my mouth as honey for sweetness (Ezekiel 3:3).

tfClaims.s: Ezekiel was commanded to lie upon his left side three hundred and ninety days.
tfClaims.why: Lie thou also upon thy left side... three hundred and ninety days (Ezekiel 4:4-5).

tfClaims.s: Daniel interpreted the handwriting on the wall.
tfClaims.why: MENE, MENE, TEKEL, UPHARSIN — this is the interpretation of the thing (Daniel 5:25-28).

tfClaims.s: Daniel's three friends came out of the fire without even the smell of flame.
tfClaims.why: Neither were their coats changed, nor had the smell of fire passed on them (Daniel 3:27).

tfClaims.s: Daniel was cast into the fiery furnace.
tfClaims.why: Daniel's three friends were cast into the furnace — Daniel was elsewhere (Daniel 3:21-26).

tfClaims.s: Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego bowed down to the golden image.
tfClaims.why: They answered: we will not serve thy gods, nor worship the golden image (Daniel 3:18).

tfClaims.s: Daniel prayed toward Babylon three times a day.
tfClaims.why: His windows being open in his chamber toward Jerusalem, he kneeled three times a day (Daniel 6:10).

tfClaims.s: Daniel's three friends were renamed Belteshazzar, Shadrach, and Meshach.
tfClaims.why: Daniel was renamed Belteshazzar; his friends were Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego (Daniel 1:7).

tfClaims.s: King Nebuchadnezzar ate grass as oxen for seven times.
tfClaims.why: He was driven from men, and did eat grass as oxen, and his body was wet with the dew of heaven (Daniel 4:33).

tfClaims.s: Belshazzar saw the fingers of a man's hand write upon the plaster of the wall.
tfClaims.why: In the same hour came forth fingers of a man's hand, and wrote over against the candlestick (Daniel 5:5).

tfClaims.s: Hosea took Gomer the daughter of Diblaim for a wife.
tfClaims.why: So he went and took Gomer the daughter of Diblaim (Hosea 1:3).

tfClaims.s: Joel prophesied that the LORD would pour out His Spirit upon all flesh.
tfClaims.why: I will pour out my spirit upon all flesh; and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy (Joel 2:28).

tfClaims.s: Joel mentions four kinds of locusts: palmerworm, locust, cankerworm, and caterpiller.
tfClaims.why: That which the palmerworm hath left hath the locust eaten; and that which the locust hath left hath the cankerworm eaten (Joel 1:4).

tfClaims.s: Amos saw a vision of the Lord standing upon a wall with a plumbline.
tfClaims.why: The Lord stood upon a wall made by a plumbline, with a plumbline in his hand (Amos 7:7).

tfClaims.s: Amos was a priest of Bethel.
tfClaims.why: I was no prophet, but an herdman of Tekoa (Amos 7:14).

tfClaims.s: Obadiah prophesied against the nation of Edom for violence against Jacob.
tfClaims.why: For thy violence against thy brother Jacob shame shall cover thee (Obadiah 1:10).

tfClaims.s: A great fish swallowed Jonah.
tfClaims.why: The LORD had prepared a great fish to swallow up Jonah (Jonah 1:17).

tfClaims.s: God sent Jonah to preach to Tarshish.
tfClaims.why: Arise, go to Nineveh — Tarshish was the port he fled to (Jonah 1:2-3).

tfClaims.s: Jonah was joyful when Nineveh repented and was spared.
tfClaims.why: It displeased Jonah exceedingly, and he was very angry (Jonah 4:1).

tfClaims.s: The men of Nineveh repented in sackcloth and ashes at Jonah's preaching.
tfClaims.why: The people of Nineveh believed God, and proclaimed a fast, and put on sackcloth (Jonah 3:5).

tfClaims.s: Micah foretold a ruler coming out of Bethlehem.
tfClaims.why: But thou, Bethlehem Ephratah — out of thee shall he come forth unto me that is to be ruler in Israel (Micah 5:2).

tfClaims.s: Micah wrote that the LORD requires man to do justly, love mercy, and walk humbly.
tfClaims.why: What doth the LORD require of thee, but to do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly? (Micah 6:8).

tfClaims.s: Nahum prophesied the total destruction of Nineveh.
tfClaims.why: The burden of Nineveh... She is empty, and void, and waste (Nahum 1:1; 2:10).

tfClaims.s: Habakkuk wrote 'the just shall live by his faith'.
tfClaims.why: Behold, his soul which is lifted up is not upright in him: but the just shall live by his faith (Habakkuk 2:4).

tfClaims.s: Habakkuk stood upon his watchtower to hear what God would speak.
tfClaims.why: I will stand upon my watch, and set me upon the tower, and will watch to see what he will say (Habakkuk 2:1).

tfClaims.s: Zephaniah prophesied that the LORD God in the midst of Zion will rejoice over her with joy.
tfClaims.why: The LORD thy God in the midst of thee is mighty; he will save, he will rejoice over thee with joy (Zephaniah 3:17).

tfClaims.s: Haggai proclaimed that the glory of the latter house shall be greater than of the former.
tfClaims.why: The glory of this latter house shall be greater than of the former, saith the LORD of hosts (Haggai 2:9).

tfClaims.s: Zechariah foretold the king coming to Jerusalem riding upon an ass.
tfClaims.why: Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Zion... thy King cometh unto thee: he is just, and having salvation; lowly, and riding upon an ass (Zechariah 9:9).

tfClaims.s: Malachi prophesied that Elijah the prophet would be sent before the great and dreadful day of the LORD.
tfClaims.why: Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the LORD (Malachi 4:5).

tfClaims.s: Malachi challenged Israel concerning robbing God in tithes and offerings.
tfClaims.why: Will a man rob God? Yet ye have robbed me. But ye say, Wherein have we robbed thee? In tithes and offerings (Malachi 3:8).

tfClaims.s: John the Baptist did eat locusts and wild honey.
tfClaims.why: His meat was locusts and wild honey (Matthew 3:4).

tfClaims.s: Andrew was Peter's brother.
tfClaims.why: The first... Andrew, and Peter his brother (Matthew 10:2).

tfClaims.s: Jesus fed five thousand with five loaves and two fishes.
tfClaims.why: Five loaves and two fishes fed five thousand men, beside women and children (Matthew 14:19-21).

tfClaims.s: The wise men offered gold, frankincense, and myrrh.
tfClaims.why: They presented unto him gifts; gold, and frankincense, and myrrh (Matthew 2:11).

tfClaims.s: Peter walked on the water to go to Jesus.
tfClaims.why: And when Peter was come down out of the ship, he walked on the water (Matthew 14:29).

tfClaims.s: Peter betrayed Jesus for thirty pieces of silver.
tfClaims.why: Judas asked the chief priests for thirty pieces of silver (Matthew 26:14-15).

tfClaims.s: Jesus fasted in the wilderness thirty days and thirty nights.
tfClaims.why: He fasted forty days and forty nights (Matthew 4:2).

tfClaims.s: John the Baptist was Andrew's brother.
tfClaims.why: Andrew was Peter's brother (Matthew 10:2).

tfClaims.s: The Sermon on the Mount was delivered in the synagogue.
tfClaims.why: He went up into a mountain — and when he was set, he taught them (Matthew 5:1-2).

tfClaims.s: Herod was glad when the wise men told him of the King of the Jews.
tfClaims.why: When Herod the king had heard these things, he was troubled (Matthew 2:3).

tfClaims.s: Pilate found Jesus guilty of treason against Rome.
tfClaims.why: Pilate said: I find no fault in this man (Luke 23:4; Matthew 27:24).

tfClaims.s: An ox and a donkey are mentioned beside the manger at Jesus's birth.
tfClaims.why: No animals are mentioned in the gospel accounts of the nativity (Luke 2:7, 16; Matthew 2:1-11).

tfClaims.s: Jesus fed the four thousand with five loaves.
tfClaims.why: The four thousand were fed with seven loaves and a few little fishes (Matthew 15:34-38).

tfClaims.s: The gospel of Matthew names three wise men.
tfClaims.why: Their number is never given — only their three gifts are named (Matthew 2:1, 11).

tfClaims.s: Barabbas was a prophet of Galilee.
tfClaims.why: Barabbas was a notable prisoner and robber (Matthew 27:16; John 18:40).

tfClaims.s: Peter denied Jesus four times before the cock crew.
tfClaims.why: Verily I say unto thee, That this night, before the cock crow, thou shalt deny me thrice (Matthew 26:34, 75).

tfClaims.s: Jesus chose ten apostles to preach the kingdom.
tfClaims.why: He called unto him his twelve disciples (Matthew 10:1).

tfClaims.s: The star stood directly over the stable in Bethlehem.
tfClaims.why: The star stood over where the young child was in a house (Matthew 2:11).

tfClaims.s: Judas cast down the thirty pieces of silver in the temple and hanged himself.
tfClaims.why: He cast down the pieces of silver in the temple, and departed, and went and hanged himself (Matthew 27:5).

tfClaims.s: Jesus stilled the storm with the words 'Peace, be still'.
tfClaims.why: And he arose, and rebuked the wind, and said unto the sea, Peace, be still (Mark 4:39).

tfClaims.s: Mark was one of the twelve apostles.
tfClaims.why: He is not in the twelve — the lists name no Mark (Matthew 10:2-4).

tfClaims.s: Bartimaeus was a blind man healed at Jericho.
tfClaims.why: Blind Bartimaeus sat by the highway side begging, and received his sight (Mark 10:46-52).

tfClaims.s: The man possessed with a legion of demons lived in the tombs.
tfClaims.why: A man with an unclean spirit, who had his dwelling among the tombs (Mark 5:2-3).

tfClaims.s: Jesus said to the daughter of Jairus, 'Talitha cumi'.
tfClaims.why: He took the damsel by the hand, and said unto her, Talitha cumi; which is, being interpreted, Damsel, I say unto thee, arise (Mark 5:41).

tfClaims.s: Mark's gospel begins with the genealogy of Jesus from Abraham.
tfClaims.why: The beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God — Matthew begins with the genealogy (Mark 1:1; Matthew 1:1).

tfClaims.s: The shepherds came with haste to the manger.
tfClaims.why: They came with haste, and found Mary and Joseph, and the babe lying in a manger (Luke 2:16).

tfClaims.s: Zacchaeus climbed up into a sycomore tree to see Jesus.
tfClaims.why: He ran before, and climbed up into a sycomore tree to see him (Luke 19:4).

tfClaims.s: The prodigal son made himself a keeper of swine.
tfClaims.why: He sent him into his fields to feed swine, and he would fain have filled his belly with husks (Luke 15:15-16).

tfClaims.s: Gabriel announced the birth of John to Zacharias in the temple.
tfClaims.why: I am Gabriel, that stand in the presence of God — thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son (Luke 1:19-20).

tfClaims.s: Luke's gospel is addressed to a man named Theophilus.
tfClaims.why: It seemed good to me also... most excellent Theophilus (Luke 1:3).

tfClaims.s: Jesus was born in Nazareth.
tfClaims.why: He was born in Bethlehem of Judaea, the city of David (Luke 2:4-7).

tfClaims.s: Zacharias doubted the angel and was struck blind.
tfClaims.why: He was struck dumb, and not able to speak, until the day John was named (Luke 1:20, 64).

tfClaims.s: The innkeeper in Bethlehem told Joseph there was no room in the inn.
tfClaims.why: The gospel says only 'there was no room for them in the inn' — an innkeeper is never mentioned (Luke 2:7).

tfClaims.s: Simeon took the infant Jesus in his arms in the temple.
tfClaims.why: Then took he him up in his arms, and blessed God (Luke 2:28).

tfClaims.s: Jesus was twelve years old when he tarried behind in Jerusalem at the temple.
tfClaims.why: When he was twelve years old... the child Jesus tarried behind in Jerusalem (Luke 2:42-43).

tfClaims.s: The good Samaritan poured in wine and vinegar into the wounded man's wounds.
tfClaims.why: Bound up his wounds, pouring in oil and wine (Luke 10:34).

tfClaims.s: The elder brother rejoiced with music and dancing when the prodigal returned.
tfClaims.why: He was angry, and would not go in (Luke 15:28).

tfClaims.s: Two disciples walked with the risen Jesus on the road to Emmaus.
tfClaims.why: Two of them went that same day to a village called Emmaus (Luke 24:13-15).

tfClaims.s: Nicodemus came to Jesus by night.
tfClaims.why: The same came to Jesus by night, and said unto him, Rabbi (John 3:2).

tfClaims.s: Mary Magdalene was the first to see the risen Jesus.
tfClaims.why: Jesus saith unto her, Mary — she turned and said Rabboni (John 20:16).

tfClaims.s: Three crosses are described on Golgotha with Jesus in the midst.
tfClaims.why: They crucified him, and two other with him, on either side one, and Jesus in the midst (John 19:18).

tfClaims.s: John's gospel begins 'In the beginning was the Word'.
tfClaims.why: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God (John 1:1).

tfClaims.s: Jesus turned water into blood at the marriage in Cana.
tfClaims.why: He turned water into wine — the first of his miracles (John 2:9, 11).

tfClaims.s: Lazarus had lain in the grave five days when Jesus called him.
tfClaims.why: By this time he stinketh: for he hath been dead four days (John 11:39).

tfClaims.s: Mary Magdalene was one of the twelve apostles.
tfClaims.why: She is never numbered among the twelve — she followed and ministered to them (Luke 8:1-3).

tfClaims.s: Caiaphas was the Roman governor of Judaea.
tfClaims.why: Pontius Pilate was governor; Caiaphas was the high priest (Matthew 27:2; John 18:13-14).

tfClaims.s: Jesus had children.
tfClaims.why: The scriptures never attribute children to Jesus — nothing in any gospel or epistle says so.

tfClaims.s: Thomas was called Didymus.
tfClaims.why: Thomas, which is called Didymus (John 11:16).

tfClaims.s: Jesus talked with a Samaritan woman at Jacob's well.
tfClaims.why: There cometh a woman of Samaria to draw water: Jesus saith unto her, Give me to drink (John 4:7).

tfClaims.s: Nathanael was sitting under a pomegranate tree when Philip called him.
tfClaims.why: Before that Philip called thee, when thou wast under the fig tree, I saw thee (John 1:48).

tfClaims.s: Paul was one of the twelve apostles.
tfClaims.why: Matthias was chosen to fill Judas' bishoprick — Paul was called later (Acts 1:26; 9:15).

tfClaims.s: Stephen wrote the book of Acts.
tfClaims.why: Acts opens as a continuation of Luke's gospel to Theophilus — Luke wrote both (Acts 1:1; Luke 1:3-4).

tfClaims.s: Paul was born in Jerusalem.
tfClaims.why: I am a man which am a Jew of Tarsus — brought up in Jerusalem (Acts 22:3).

tfClaims.s: Paul was thrown from a horse on the road to Damascus.
tfClaims.why: He fell to the earth, but scripture never mentions a horse or mount (Acts 9:4).

tfClaims.s: Pentecost fell upon the disciples in Galilee.
tfClaims.why: They were all with one accord in one place at Jerusalem (Acts 2:1, 14).

tfClaims.s: The believers were called Christians first in Rome.
tfClaims.why: The disciples were called Christians first in Antioch (Acts 11:26).

tfClaims.s: About three hundred souls were added to the church on the day of Pentecost.
tfClaims.why: There were added unto them that day about three thousand souls (Acts 2:41).

tfClaims.s: Romans was addressed to the church at Corinth.
tfClaims.why: To all that be at Rome — beloved of God, called to be saints (Romans 1:7).

tfClaims.s: The phrase 'God helps those who help themselves' is found in the epistles of Paul.
tfClaims.why: This is a secular proverb from antiquity, not found in the scriptures.

tfClaims.s: Paul says he was baptized by Peter in Corinth.
tfClaims.why: I thank God that I baptized none of you, but Crispus and Gaius (1 Corinthians 1:14).

tfClaims.s: Galatians teaches that a man is justified by the works of the law.
tfClaims.why: Knowing that a man is not justified by the works of the law, but by the faith of Jesus Christ (Galatians 2:16).

tfClaims.s: Ephesians teaches that salvation is earned by works.
tfClaims.why: For by grace are ye saved through faith... not of works, lest any man should boast (Ephesians 2:8-9).

tfClaims.s: Paul wrote Philippians from a palace in Babylon.
tfClaims.why: Paul wrote from his bonds in prison in Rome (Philippians 1:13).

tfClaims.s: Paul wrote that money itself is the root of all evil.
tfClaims.why: The LOVE of money is the root — not money itself (1 Timothy 6:10).

tfClaims.s: The epistle to the Hebrews names Paul as its author in the opening verse.
tfClaims.why: Hebrews opens with God speaking by his Son — no human author is named (Hebrews 1:1-2).

tfClaims.s: The Revelation was given to Peter.
tfClaims.why: The Revelation of Jesus Christ... unto his servant John (Revelation 1:1).

tfClaims.s: The number of the beast is six hundred sixteen.
tfClaims.why: It is six hundred threescore and six — 666 (Revelation 13:18).

tfClaims.s: The seven seals of Revelation are opened by the archangel Michael.
tfClaims.why: The Lion of the tribe of Juda, the Lamb, opened the seals (Revelation 5:5; 6:1).
